summary: George Uglow Pope (1820–1908) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as head of Breeks Memorial School (1859–1870) and Bishop Cotton Boys' School (1870), and later held posts at the University of Oxford from 1883.

George V. Bobrinskoy (1901–1985) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Lutheran Theological Seminary, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale under Franklin Edgerton. He taught at Yale (1927–1928) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Chicago (1951–1967).

George Watt (1851–1930) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Marischal College, Aberdeen, and the University of Glasgow. His career included posts as Professor of Botany at Presidency University (1873–1874) and lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (~1907–1909).

George Weston Briggs (1874–1966), an Indologist and religious studies scholar, earned a B.S. from Northwestern University. He taught at Lucknow Christian College (~1903–1915) and later served at Drew University as Professor of Sanskrit (1925) and History of Religions (1929–1944).

George William Brown (1870–1932) specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hiram College and earned a Ph.D. from Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He later held professorships at the College of Missions (1921) and Lexington Theological Seminary (1927–1932).

George de Roerich (1902–1960) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Harvard and the University of Paris under scholars including Lanman and Lévi. He directed the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute and taught at Moscow State University.

George van Driem (born 1957) is a scholar in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Leiden University. He held the Chair for Descriptive Linguistics at Leiden (1996–2009) and the Chair of Historical Linguistics at the University of Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, Ganden Shartse Monastery, and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He served as a professor of religion at Williams College (~1992–2003).

Georges Cuendet (1897–1980) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Geneva under Charles Bally and at EPHE under Antoine Meillet. He taught at Gymnase de Nyon (~1926–1962) and served as Privatdozent of Indology at the University of Geneva (1938–1963).

Georges Dandoy (1882–1962) was a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Namur, Stonyhurst, Oxford, and St. Mary's College, Kurseong. He held posts at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1909–1912), and St. Mary's College, Kurseong (1917–1922).

Georges Dumézil (1898–1986) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet, he held posts at Istanbul University (1925–1931), EPHE (1935–1968), and the Collège de France (1949–1968).

Georges Guieysse (1869–1889) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under prominent teachers including Sylvain Lévi, Michel Bréal, Abel Bergaigne, Ferdinand de Saussure, and James Darmesteter.

Georges Perrot (1832–1914) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1852. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1874–1883), the University of Paris (~1877–1883), and directed the ENS (~1883–1904).

Georges Redard (1922–2005) worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Neuchâtel under Max Jakob Niedermann, Bern, and Paris under Émile Benveniste. He taught at Neuchâtel and became extraordinary Professor at the University of Bern in 1954.

Georges Strehly (1851–1906) was an Indology scholar who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, the Sorbonne, and the EPHE under Abel Bergaigne and Paul Regnaud. He taught at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1879–1886) and Lycée Louis-le-Grand (1886–1906).

Georges-Jean Pinault (born 1955) is a specialist in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, EPHE, and under Jean Haudry, he served as professor at Blaise Pascal University (~1985–1996) and EPHE from 1999.

Georgij Aleksandrovič Zograf (1928–1993) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov and Vasilij Matveevič Beskrovnyj. He held research positions at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences from 1954.

Georgij Saridanovič Ahvlediani (1887–1973) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kharkiv and Saint Petersburg under Knauer, Salemann, and Shcherbatskoy. He was Professor at Tbilisi State University and directed the Georgian Institute of Linguistics (1949–1950).

Georgios Kozakis Typaldos (1790–1867) was an Indology scholar who studied medicine at the University of Padua. He served as Librarian at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens from approximately 1836 to 1863.

Georgios Nikolaou Hatzidakis (1848–1941) was a linguist who studied at Athens, Leipzig, Jena, and Berlin under Windisch, Brugmann, and Delbrück. He served as Rector of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (1926) and President of the Academy of Athens (1927).
